body:
Minutes:

- Grid Navigation Issue Status: Tab Atkins-Bittner opens a discussion on the grid navigation issue initiated by Yujac. Someone from Microsoft notes that Yujac is currently on vacation, and a discussion ensues regarding whether the proposal is tracked via a pull request or an issue, with Anne van Kesteren and Olli Pettay seeking clarification on the documentation. The group reaches a consensus to hold off on further discussion until Yujac returns ([00:02:09](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1F3xGrWYFQs8fVAgEzMKtk9HUjXtO2KBfvTj-pqHy4Wk/edit?resourcekey=0-MdhTIHUrf3LwjYtN2a-RNA&tab=t.r6c1ohmffyz0#heading=h.p0lknpfijy4u)).
- Media Element Remove Text Track Method: Dana Estra presents pull request proposals for adding a `removeTextTrack` method to media elements, raising the open question of whether it should be restricted to JavaScript-added text tracks or also permit the removal of track elements and inband tracks. Jer Noble shares Apple's perspective that the method should be restricted because track elements are already removable via the Document Object Model, whereas inband tracks (such as embedded 608 or 708 captions in an MP4 file) are extremely complex to remove as media parsers continually emit new samples. Brian Kardell, Anne van Kesteren, and Simon Pieters discuss implementation details and potential error handling, while Noam Rosenthal notes that Dale Curtis from Chrome finds the restriction sensible. The group reaches a consensus to narrowly restrict the method to JavaScript-added text tracks and throw an error for other track types to reduce implementation complexity ([00:04:42](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1F3xGrWYFQs8fVAgEzMKtk9HUjXtO2KBfvTj-pqHy4Wk/edit?resourcekey=0-MdhTIHUrf3LwjYtN2a-RNA&tab=t.r6c1ohmffyz0#heading=h.sav1mifkndb2)).
- Module Stylesheet Link Tags: Kurt Catti-Schmidt introduces pull request 12339 regarding a new explainer for module stylesheet fetching using link tags with `rel="stylesheet" type="module"` and specifier href attributes that go through import map processing. Anne van Kesteren raises concerns about overloading the link element's type attribute and whether bare specifiers conflict with standard URL parsing. Noam Rosenthal, Kurt Catti-Schmidt, Ryosuke Niwa, and Simon Pieters discuss alternative approaches, including script elements, style tag attributes, fallback mechanisms via on-error handlers, and sanitizer security implications where script elements present higher risks. Ultimately, Kurt Catti-Schmidt asks participants to review the pull request and leave feedback on the issue ([00:14:34](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1F3xGrWYFQs8fVAgEzMKtk9HUjXtO2KBfvTj-pqHy4Wk/edit?resourcekey=0-MdhTIHUrf3LwjYtN2a-RNA&tab=t.r6c1ohmffyz0#heading=h.tf75j6r3meqi)).
- New Menu Elements and Field Set Grouping: David Baron presents pull request 12011 for new menu elements, asking the group to review whether it is ready for stage three. Olli Pettay and Anne van Kesteren question the requirement to use field set elements to group checkbox and radio menu items, suggesting alternative attributes like name or making the container optional. David Baron and Luke defend the field set requirement, explaining that it prevents poor authoring practices that separate checkable items, which creates severe accessibility and keyboard navigation issues. Simon Pieters also inquires about potential default cascading style sheets styling issues associated with field sets. The group concludes that participants should review the explainer and provide feedback on the pull request ([00:32:34](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1F3xGrWYFQs8fVAgEzMKtk9HUjXtO2KBfvTj-pqHy4Wk/edit?resourcekey=0-MdhTIHUrf3LwjYtN2a-RNA&tab=t.r6c1ohmffyz0#heading=h.epslhb56wn4i)).
- HTML and Canvas Updates: someone in Philip Rogers provides an update on HTML and canvas features, outlining four primary changes: supporting the drawing of arbitrary descendants to better integrate with cascading style sheets and HTML frameworks, improving synchronization between the Document Object Model and drawn content, integrating feedback from the accessibility working group to support standard accessibility primitives like inert, and aligning the application programming interface with feedback from the WebGL and WebGPU working groups. Tab Atkins-Bittner notes time constraints, and someone in Philip Rogers requests that participants review the updated design, specification pull request, explainer, and implementation, and file new issues as needed ([00:47:41](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1F3xGrWYFQs8fVAgEzMKtk9HUjXtO2KBfvTj-pqHy4Wk/edit?resourcekey=0-MdhTIHUrf3LwjYtN2a-RNA&tab=t.r6c1ohmffyz0#heading=h.iu6bcs9ad2ap)).
